title: Wine Wimsey Review · Oct 23
subtitle: 12 feed posts (all 12 inbox images rebuilt as Wine Wimsey cartoons, quotes word for word, no TOBIs today) and 4 stories I wrote myself · Hot Mess and Homebody split evenly · Flags: #1 and #6 have wine in the quote itself · #9 is close to an earlier menopause post · #12 and #3 are rebuilds of other pages' memes, branding left out

posts.quote: I quit jogging because I kept spilling my wine
posts.caption: I caught myself jogging last spring. It wasn't planned. The mail carrier was leaving and I had a package to hand her, so I ran, and about forty feet later I understood why I had never done it before. A woman passed me pushing a stroller and a golden retriever on a leash, and she wasn't even sweating. I took the nearest bench to think it over and have been working through my options ever since. The bench has a great view and no schedule. I call it a recovery program.
posts.first: My sister signed me up for a 5K once. I walked it, mostly. A man dressed as a hot dog finished ahead of me and I have made peace with that. They handed me a banana at the finish line and I ate it like I'd won something. Best part of the whole morning.

posts.quote: People my age are climbing mountains and ziplining. Me? I got both legs into my underwear without tipping over. Frankly, I'm crushing it.
posts.caption: My neighbor just got back from a glacier hike. I just got back from the bedroom. We are both exhausted and we both deserve a snack.
posts.first: I did a victory lap around the dresser afterward with one hand on the wall for balance. The laundry basket was the only witness. It has never once been impressed by me, but I'm choosing to believe it was a little proud this time.

posts.quote: Getting older is using your phone's flashlight to read the menu, then discovering you have taken fourteen photographs of your own chin.
posts.caption: The waiter came by three times. Each time I was holding my phone over the menu like a crime scene investigator, and each time he left quietly. I finally ordered by pointing at the third thing on the page. It turned out to be the children's meal, and it arrived with a crayon. I colored the entire placemat while I waited. A man at the next table asked if I was a food critic. I said no, just a customer with a plan that did not survive the lighting.
posts.first: My daughter gave me a pair of reading glasses with a little light built in. I wore them to dinner once and a stranger asked if I was a miner. I told her I was off the clock. We ended up splitting a dessert.

posts.quote: If they can pay someone to stand there watching me scan my own groceries, they can pay someone to run a real checkout.
posts.caption: I stood at the self-checkout on Saturday while the machine told me for the fourth time that there was an unexpected item in the bagging area. There was not. It was a banana. The attendant walked over, tapped one button, and walked away without a word, which means she had that power the whole time. I paid, bagged my own groceries, and thanked the machine on the way out, out of habit. It said nothing back, which was the most professional exchange I had all day.
posts.first: My mother worked the same register for thirty years and knew every customer by name. Last week I asked the machine to please be patient with me. It said please wait for assistance. We are not close, but we are working on something.

posts.caption: I stood in the produce aisle for four minutes holding a bag of spinach and a candy bar like a scale at the county fair. A man reached around me for a cucumber and apologized. I apologized back. The candy bar won on points.

posts.quote: Retirement age should be 50. People deserve more time to live... Not just work until they're too old and tired to enjoy it.
posts.caption: My father worked at the same plant for thirty-four years and retired at sixty-six with a bad shoulder and a lawn chair. He used the lawn chair twice before his knees stopped cooperating. I think about that more than I should. These days I plan my day around the good hours, the window between the second cup of coffee and the afternoon slump when I'm actually useful. I'm trying to waste them very deliberately by the fire.
posts.first: My dad finally took his first real vacation at sixty-seven. He packed three days early and checked the weather every morning for a week. He came home and said the best part was the drive back, because now he could say he'd done it. I laughed. He wasn't joking.

posts.quote: Managing menopause simply requires drinking more water, sleeping eight hours, exercising daily, avoiding sugar, reducing stress and staying positive. I can't imagine why anyone is struggling.
posts.caption: I keep a small battery fan in my purse and another in the glove compartment, and I treat both like emergency equipment. The one in the laundry room has a name. At two on Tuesday afternoon my face did something I can only describe as a sunrise, and I stood in front of the open freezer case at the grocery store like a woman with a plan. Nobody stopped me. A stock boy offered me a pamphlet, which I took, because I'm polite and also hot.
posts.first: My friend Denise says it's hormones. My other friend says it's the house. My mother says it was exactly like this for her and she just wore a lighter cardigan. I've decided they're all right and I'm still hot. The fan stays on.

posts.quote: My brain now treats new information like Snapchat. Gone in seconds.
posts.caption: I sat down to write myself a note about the thing I needed to remember. I wrote remember the thing. Then I stuck it on the wall with eleven other notes that say similar things. The wall is yellow now. Yesterday I called my sister to ask about the thing, and she said she has no idea what the thing is, but she hopes it went well.
posts.first: I put a sticky note on the fridge that says check the other sticky note. I'm proud of that one. It works about half the time, and half is a passing grade in this house. The pen I used to write it is still missing.

posts.quote: That first sip of coffee. A sacred little ceremony before the daily tomfoolery.
posts.caption: My mother had a rule that nobody spoke to her until the cup was half gone. I come from a long line of women with a very simple morning protocol.
posts.first: The first time my neighbor tried to chat before my first sip, I held up one finger and kept my eyes closed until it was done. She waited. She has since started bringing her own mug and sitting in silence beside me. It's the best friendship I've ever had.
